caption:
Elon Musk's AI company launched The X Subscription, one plan for Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor and X Premium.
The $30 Premium tier bundles benefits that used to cost $90 a month.
But rival models like Claude in Cursor are now billed separately at API prices.

Would you pay $30 for Grok, Cursor and X in one plan?

slides.headline: Elon Musk just put Grok, Cursor and X into one plan, and *Claude now costs extra*

slides.heading: One plan, *four products*
paras: X launched The X Subscription on October 12. It bundles Grok, Grok Bot, the Cursor coding app and X Premium into one plan.
There are five tiers: Free, Plus at $8, Premium at $30, Super at $100 and Ultra at $200 a month.

slides.heading: The *$30* sweet spot
paras: Premium includes the benefits of SuperGrok, Cursor Pro and X Premium+, which xAI says previously cost $90 a month combined.
Paid plans share one pool of Grok usage across the Grok apps, the Grok tab on X and Cursor.

slides.heading: Claude *costs extra* now
paras: Third-party models in Cursor now start at Premium. Their usage is billed separately at API list prices through top-ups.
The New Stack's example: a user spending $20 on Claude under the old $20 plan would now pay $50 a month.

slides.heading: Old plans *stay for now*
paras: Existing SuperGrok, Cursor and X Premium subscribers can keep their current plans or switch with a prorated refund.

paras.t: "Nothing happens to your Pro plan automatically," a SpaceXAI support engineer wrote.

slides.hook: Musk wants one subscription for chat, code and social. Follow to see if it pulls coders away from Claude and ChatGPT.
